{"full_contract_with_original_span_markers":"<SPAN 0>CONFIDENTIALITY, NON-DISCLOSURE AND COMPUTER ACCESS (SECURITY) AGREEMENT</SPAN 0>
<SPAN 1>“Responsibilities”</SPAN 1>
<SPAN 2>A. Every person who has been given access to a University of Nebraska information system or who has access to or knowledge of confidential or sensitive information or data, is obligated to keep such data confidential. </SPAN 2><SPAN 3>Accordingly, every University of Nebraska employee, student, volunteer, contractor, business associate, or guest who either has or will be given access to printed or online confidential data is required to read and acknowledge his or her understanding of this agreement before being granted access.</SPAN 3>
<SPAN 4>1. I will only access confidential or sensitive data for legitimate business purposes as permitted by the University and will not use confidential or sensitive data for personal use. </SPAN 4><SPAN 5>I understand that confidential or sensitive data includes but is not limited to databases and records containing Social Security numbers, checking and savings account numbers, non-published telephone numbers, personnel appraisals, educational records, medical history, and insurance coverage information.</SPAN 5>
<SPAN 6>2. I will not leave confidential or sensitive data in view of others who do not have a legitimate business reason to view the data and I will only share confidential data with persons having authorized access.</SPAN 6>
<SPAN 7>3. I will not discuss confidential or sensitive information or data in public places and will not remove confidential or sensitive data from my work site without University authorization.</SPAN 7>
<SPAN 8>NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT</SPAN 8>
<SPAN 9>B. As an employee, contractor or consultant of the University of Nebraska, and related to my job responsibilities or assigned tasks, I may have access to, come in contact with, or reference confidential or sensitive information or data. </SPAN 9><SPAN 10>Examples of this information and data include, but are not limited to: passwords, student disciplinary and academic records, personal health information, medical and research data, Social Security numbers, legally protected information, financial reports, security parameters and configurations, payroll information and personnel records, system logs and network traffic data, etc. </SPAN 10><SPAN 11>This information or data is subject to University policies as well as regulatory and special handling requirements.</SPAN 11>
<SPAN 12>1. I accept responsibility for appropriate handling and management of information and data whether I come into contact with such information through my authorized access or in error.</SPAN 12>
<SPAN 13>2. I will maintain the conﬁdentiality of this information and if uncertain about the appropriateness of who this information may be shared with in the course of my authorized access, I will discuss any questions I have with my supervisor or the Central Administration security oﬃce. </SPAN 13><SPAN 14>I understand that even the most innocuous ﬁle can contain conﬁdential information.</SPAN 14>
<SPAN 15>3. In all instances as described above, I acknowledge my personal obligation to protect, through execution of reasonable steps, the confidentiality, integrity and privacy of this data in accordance with University policies, regulatory requirements or other special handling requirements, and prevent unauthorized access, modification, destruction or disclosure of sensitive or confidential data. </SPAN 15><SPAN 16>In the absence of stated guidance or without a clear indication of sensitivity, I will treat and handle all data as if it were sensitive.</SPAN 16>
<SPAN 17>C. Acknowledgement</SPAN 17>
<SPAN 18>1. I have read and understand the statements presented in the above “Responsibilities” section regarding my permitted and potential/inadvertent access to confidential or sensitive information or data.</SPAN 18>
<SPAN 19>2. I agree with these stated responsibilities.</SPAN 19>
<SPAN 20>3. I understand that misuse of confidential or sensitive information or data, whether intentional or due to neglect on my part, is a breach of policy and grounds for corrective action which may include my dismissal, the termination of access to University resources, or the termination of a contractual agreement and may subject me to possible civil and/or criminal legal action.</SPAN 20>
<SPAN 21>D. During the course of my work or activities at the University of Nebraska, I may be assigned a computer user login ID and instructed to develop personal passwords. </SPAN 21><SPAN 22>In order to maintain the confidentiality of non-public data, I agree to the following:</SPAN 22>
<SPAN 23>1. I will adhere to the University of Nebraska’s Executive Memorandum No. 16, Policy for Responsible Use of University Computers and Information Systems, University of Nebraska’s Executive Memorandum No. 26, Information Security Plan, and to any additional specific policies that I may be asked to follow.</SPAN 23>
<SPAN 24>2. I will obtain authorization from the University prior to gaining access to those specific computer functions necessary to perform my responsibilities.</SPAN 24>
<SPAN 25>3. I will not share my computer user login IDs and passwords with anyone, at any time, for any reason, except in cases necessary to facilitate computer maintenance and repairs.</SPAN 25>
<SPAN 26>4. I will not leave a terminal, personal computer or computer workstation without locking or ending any application that either contains or can be used to access confidential or sensitive information or data.</SPAN 26>
<SPAN 27>5. I will not disclose any budget, financial, personnel, payroll or procurement information except to the extent necessary to carry out the responsibilities of my employment or as otherwise required by the law.</SPAN 27>
<SPAN 28>6. I will contact the University immediately if I discover that my computer user login ID or password has been compromised, if I suspect that University digital asset has been misused, or if I suspect that someone has obtained unauthorized access to confidential or sensitive information or data on the University of Nebraska information system.</SPAN 28>
<SPAN 29> </SPAN 29><SPAN 30>7. I also understand that improper use of my computer user login ID or password is a breach of policy and grounds for corrective action which may include dismissal, the termination of access to University resources, or the termination of a contractual agreement and may subject me to possible civil and/or criminal legal action.</SPAN 30>

<SPAN 34>Person to be granted access</SPAN 34>

Okay, let's tackle this query step by step. The user provided a detailed NDA document with various hypotheses and wants me to determine for each whether it's an Entailment, Contradiction, or NotMentioned based on the document. 

First, I need to understand each hypothesis and check the document for relevant sections. Let me start with the first hypothesis, nda-11: "Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer any objects which embody Disclosing Party's Confidential Information." Looking through the document, I don't see any mention of reverse engineering. The document talks about confidentiality, non-disclosure, and handling data, but not reverse engineering specifically. So this would be NotMentioned.

Next, nda-16: "Receiving Party shall destroy or return some Confidential Information upon the termination of Agreement." The document mentions in section 20 that misuse is a breach, but there's no explicit mention of destroying or returning info upon termination. So NotMentioned again.

For nda-15: "Agreement shall not grant Receiving Party any right to Confidential Information." The document states that the Receiving Party must keep data confidential and not use it for personal purposes. However, it doesn't explicitly say there's no right granted. It might be implied, but since the document doesn't explicitly state this, it's NotMentioned.

nda-10: "Receiving Party shall not disclose the fact that Agreement was agreed or negotiated." The document's Non-Disclosure Agreement section (section 8) mentions not disclosing confidential information, but not the existence of the agreement itself. So NotMentioned.

nda-2: "Confidential Information shall only include technical information." The document lists examples in section 10, which include non-technical data like personal health info and financial records. So this is contradicted by the examples given. Therefore, Contradiction.

nda-1: "All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified by the Disclosing Party." The document doesn't mention that the Disclosing Party must explicitly identify the information. It just talks about what constitutes confidential data. So NotMentioned.

nda-19: "Some obligations of Agreement may survive termination of Agreement." The document mentions consequences for misuse after termination (section 20), which implies some obligations remain. So Entailment.

nda-12: "Receiving Party may independently develop information similar to Confidential Information." The document doesn't prohibit this, so it's allowed. Hence, Entailment.

nda-20: "Receiving Party may retain some Confidential Information even after the return or destruction of Confidential Information." The document doesn't mention retention post-termination, so NotMentioned.

nda-3: "Confidential Information may include verbally conveyed information." Section 10 lists examples that include verbal info like personal health info, so this is supported. Entailment.

nda-18: "Receiving Party shall not solicit some of Disclosing Party's representatives." The document doesn't mention solicitation, so NotMentioned.

nda-7: "Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some third-parties." Section 6 allows sharing with authorized persons, which could include third parties. So Entailment.

nda-17: "Receiving Party may create a copy of some Confidential Information in some circumstances." The document doesn't mention copying, so NotMentioned.

nda-8: "Receiving Party shall notify Disclosing Party in case Receiving Party is required by law to disclose any Confidential Information." The document doesn't mention legal disclosure requirements, so NotMentioned.

nda-13: "Receiving Party may acquire information similar to Confidential Information from a third party." The document doesn't address this, so NotMentioned.
